title: Algorithmic Thinking and Correctness
summary: What an algorithm is, how to describe one precisely, and how to argue it is correct using loop invariants — the mental tools every later lesson relies on.

title: Big-O and Complexity Analysis
summary: Asymptotic notation (O, Ω, Θ), best/average/worst case, and amortized vs. worst-case — how to reason about time and space as input size grows.

title: Arrays and Dynamic Arrays
summary: Contiguous storage and O(1) indexing, and how a dynamic array (Python's list) grows to give amortized O(1) append.

title: Linked Lists
summary: Singly and doubly linked lists, the node/pointer model, and the O(1)-insert / O(n)-search trade-off that distinguishes them from arrays.

title: Stacks and Queues
summary: LIFO stacks and FIFO queues, their array- and linked-backed implementations, Python's deque, and where each shows up in real algorithms.

title: Hash Tables
summary: Hashing, collision resolution (chaining vs. open addressing), load factor, and why lookups are O(1) average but O(n) worst case — the engine behind Python's dict and set.

title: Recursion and the Call Stack
summary: Base and recursive cases, how the call stack holds each frame, recursion vs. iteration, and the stack-depth limits you must respect in Python.

title: Elementary Sorting: Bubble, Selection, Insertion
summary: The three quadratic sorts, what stability and in-place mean, and why insertion sort is the one you'll actually reach for on small or nearly-sorted data.

title: Linear and Binary Search
summary: Sequential search, and binary search with its sorted-input precondition, O(log n) cost, notorious off-by-one bugs, and Python's bisect module.

title: Divide and Conquer and Merge Sort
summary: The divide-and-conquer paradigm and merge sort — its stable, guaranteed O(n log n) behaviour, the merge step, and the recurrence that explains the bound.

title: Quicksort
summary: Partitioning (Lomuto and Hoare), quicksort's average O(n log n) vs. worst-case O(n²), why randomization matters, and how it compares with merge sort.

title: Heaps and Heapsort
summary: The binary heap and its array layout, sift-up/sift-down, O(n) build-heap, heapsort, and priority queues via Python's heapq.

title: Binary Search Trees
summary: The BST property, search/insert/delete, in-order traversal, and why an unbalanced tree can degrade from O(log n) to O(n).

title: Balanced Trees: AVL and Red-Black
summary: How rotations keep a search tree's height O(log n) — the AVL and red-black balancing schemes, and where self-balancing trees are used in practice.

title: Graph Representations and Traversal (BFS & DFS)
summary: Adjacency lists vs. matrices, and breadth-first and depth-first search — O(V+E) traversals that underpin connectivity, shortest paths, and cycle detection.

title: Non-Comparison Sorting: Counting, Radix, Bucket
summary: Counting, radix, and bucket sort — how sorting by key structure instead of comparisons beats the Ω(n log n) comparison lower bound, and when it applies.

title: Dynamic Programming I: Foundations
summary: Optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems, memoization vs. tabulation, worked on Fibonacci, coin change, and the 0/1 knapsack.

title: Dynamic Programming II: Classic Problems
summary: Longest common subsequence, edit distance, and longest increasing subsequence — building the DP table and reconstructing the optimal solution.

title: Greedy Algorithms
summary: The greedy-choice property and optimal substructure, worked on activity selection and Huffman coding — and a clear look at when greedy fails and DP is required.

title: Shortest Paths: Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford
summary: Single-source shortest paths: Dijkstra with a heap for non-negative weights, and Bellman-Ford for graphs with negative edges and negative-cycle detection.

title: Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal and Prim
summary: The cut property and two greedy MST algorithms — Kruskal with union-find and Prim with a heap — plus why both produce a minimum spanning tree.

title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
summary: The disjoint-set data structure with union by rank/size and path compression, its near-constant amortized cost, and its role in Kruskal and connectivity.

title: Backtracking
summary: Systematic search with pruning — building solutions incrementally and abandoning dead ends — worked on subsets, permutations, and the N-Queens problem.

title: String Matching: Naive and KMP
summary: Finding a pattern in text: the naive O(nm) scan versus Knuth–Morris–Pratt's O(n+m) using the prefix function, with a note on Rabin–Karp's rolling hash.
